chapter: Minton's, bop and the Monk circle
title: Monk's rehearsal big band and the real beginning of bebop
summary: Monk and Bud Powell rehearsed in a basement to create a new music for recognition; she says Dizzy created real bebop and Monk worked for Dizzy.

story.theme_name: Charlie Parker, Dizzy and the bebop revolution
story.community_name: Playing with and understanding Thelonious Monk

blocks.x: Was this the time that Monk had tried to start a big band?

He did start it, because everybody used to pitch in 50¢ or do arrangements and often I gave them money. They used to rehearse in the basement of some place, but the whole idea was, you know, like our black people never get credit, receive credit for anything they do or create. So what they were doing, they created a new music as far as Monk is concerned in order to get some kind of recognition for us, so they stayed in this cellar - basement - and rehearsed as long as they could and then they'd come out and try to get jobs. Then everybody copied it; they lost again.
The real beginnings of bebop then were in this big band that Monk had organized?

Yes. Well, I'll say Dizzy was the real beginning. It happened to be an era of music that everybody played, like boogie-woogie. Every kid born playing something played boogie-woogie. I heard Monk play but he wasn't actually playing the real bebop. It was Dizzy that created the real bebop.
Was Dizzy in Monk's big band?
